The featured products range from budget‑friendly Wi‑Fi cameras to high‑end, subscription‑based systems, all designed to provide real‑time alerts, two‑way audio, and cloud‑based video storage. The article notes that each device was tested for reliability, ease of installation, and integration with popular smart‑home ecosystems such as Alexa, Google Assistant, and Apple HomeKit.

Key details include the Ring Video Doorbell Pro 2, which offers 1530‑ppi video and a 180‑degree field of view, and the Nest Hello, known for its facial‑detection algorithm that can distinguish between familiar faces and strangers. More affordable options like the Eufy Security Wi‑Fi Video Doorbell deliver comparable image quality without a subscription fee, while the Arlo Essential Video Doorbell adds motion‑based alerts and a built‑in siren. Prices range from $80 for entry‑level models to $250 for premium units, and the article emphasizes that most devices support encrypted data transmission and optional cloud storage plans.

In conclusion, WIRED’s testing confirms that the right front‑door monitor can drastically reduce missed deliveries and enhance home security. Whether a homeowner prefers a subscription‑based service with advanced analytics or a one‑time purchase with local storage, the reviewed devices provide reliable, remote access to the front door, ensuring peace of mind no matter where the user is.
author: Wired

title: Ugreen Unveils MagFlow Pro: $149.99 Power Bank with Liquid Cooling and Wireless Charging
content:
Ugreen has announced the launch of its MagFlow Pro Magnetic Power Bank, a high‑end portable charger that promises to bring industrial‑grade cooling to everyday devices. Priced at $149.99, the unit packs a 10,000 mAh battery and claims to be the world’s first power bank equipped with a liquid‑cooling system that works in tandem with Qi 2.2‑compatible wireless charging.

The MagFlow Pro incorporates several novel features that set it apart from conventional power banks. Its CryoPulse technology uses a micro‑pump to circulate a coolant through the internal circuitry, actively drawing heat away from the battery and the wireless charging coil. The device also boasts a “Cyber Window,” a transparent panel that displays real‑time temperature and charging metrics. Together, these elements aim to reduce heat buildup, potentially extending battery life and improving safety during high‑power output.

Available now, the MagFlow Pro targets tech enthusiasts and professionals who require reliable, high‑performance charging on the go. While its price sits at the upper end of the market, the combination of magnetic docking, liquid cooling, and wireless charging positions it as a niche option for users willing to invest in cutting‑edge power management. For more details, see the full story on The Verge.
author: The Verge

title: Primates’ Diarrhea Outbreak Provides New Targets for Shigella Vaccine Development
content:
Researchers have identified new molecular targets that could accelerate the development of a vaccine against Shigella, the bacterium responsible for millions of diarrheal illnesses worldwide each year. In a recent study published in *Nature Microbiology*, scientists used high‑throughput proteomics and reverse vaccinology to pinpoint a set of surface‑exposed proteins that elicit strong, cross‑reactive antibody responses in animal models. The team also mapped the genetic loci that regulate the expression of these proteins, revealing potential regulatory checkpoints that could be exploited to enhance vaccine efficacy.

The findings provide a clearer roadmap for vaccine designers, who can now focus on these conserved antigens rather than the highly variable surface structures that have historically thwarted vaccine efforts. By incorporating these targets into subunit or conjugate vaccine platforms, researchers anticipate improved protection against multiple Shigella serotypes. The study’s authors emphasize that the insights into host‑pathogen interactions also open avenues for adjunct therapies that block bacterial invasion pathways.

With these new targets in hand, the field moves closer to a broadly protective Shigella vaccine. The next steps involve preclinical testing of candidate formulations and assessing their safety and immunogenicity in larger animal models, paving the way for eventual human trials.
author: Ars Technica

title: Xbox Adds Time Limits to Game Pass Streaming
content:
Microsoft has announced that more than one million active Game Pass subscribers will face increased fees for heavy streaming use. The change follows a review of the service’s bandwidth consumption, with Microsoft citing rising costs for cloud infrastructure and the need to maintain performance for all users. Subscribers who exceed the current data thresholds will be charged an additional fee on top of their standard subscription rate.

The new policy applies to both Xbox Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass plans, and will be implemented in the coming weeks. Microsoft has stated that the additional charges will be transparent and calculated based on actual data usage, rather than a flat rate. The company also indicated that it will continue to invest in network optimization to minimize the impact on casual gamers. The move has drawn mixed reactions from the community, with some users expressing concern over the cost of high‑definition streaming while others welcome the effort to sustain service quality.
author: Ars Technica

title: CDC Staff Accepted Measles Death Reports Before RFK Jr. Intervention
content:
The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) confirmed a series of measles‑related deaths in the United States earlier this year, citing data from state health departments and hospital records. According to CDC officials, the agency had already reviewed and accepted the death reports before former U.S. Senator Robert F. Kennedy Jr. publicly questioned the findings. The agency’s epidemiologists had documented the cases as part of its routine surveillance of vaccine‑preventable diseases.

Kennedy, who has long been a vocal critic of the measles‑mumps‑rubella (MMR) vaccine, released statements on social media and in interviews suggesting that the CDC’s reporting was inaccurate or incomplete. In his remarks, he called for a re‑examination of the data and implied that the agency might have misrepresented the severity of the outbreak. However, CDC staff maintained that the data had been validated through established protocols and that the deaths were consistent with known complications of measles.

The CDC has reiterated its commitment to transparent reporting and continues to monitor measles cases nationwide. While the agency has not issued a formal response to Kennedy’s claims, it emphasized that its surveillance data are subject to peer review and are used to guide public health interventions. The situation highlights ongoing tensions between public health authorities and vaccine skeptics, underscoring the importance of evidence‑based communication in disease control efforts.
author: Ars Technica

title: Startup ARR Declines as AI Disrupts Enterprise Buying
content:
The rapid adoption of generative AI and other advanced machine‑learning tools has reshaped the procurement landscape for large enterprises. Decision‑makers now prioritize speed, scalability, and integration capabilities, often favoring cloud‑native solutions that can be deployed in weeks rather than months. This shift has disrupted traditional vendor relationships, compressed sales cycles, and increased demand for real‑time analytics and compliance monitoring.

Startups, many of which have built their value propositions around AI‑driven products, find themselves at a crossroads. While they possess the agility to innovate, they lack the established sales networks and long‑term contracts that secure enterprise contracts. Moreover, the new buying criteria—such as data sovereignty, regulatory compliance, and multi‑tenant architecture—require expertise that many early‑stage companies have yet to develop. As a result, a growing number of startups are partnering with larger incumbents or forming strategic alliances to gain credibility and access to enterprise buyers.

Industry analysts predict that the next wave of AI‑focused startups will need to adopt a hybrid approach: maintaining their core innovation while building robust compliance frameworks and scalable deployment models. Companies that can demonstrate clear ROI, secure data handling, and seamless integration with existing enterprise ecosystems will be best positioned to capture the fragmented market created by the AI‑driven shift in buying patterns.
author: TechCrunch

title: Tesla Seeks Cybercab Fleet Buyers
content:
A technology firm announced on Thursday that it has added a new online form to its website to collect contact information from individuals and organizations interested in purchasing Cybercab fleet vehicles. The solicitation, posted on the company’s official site, invites prospective buyers to submit basic details such as name, company affiliation, and intended vehicle quantity, with the aim of facilitating follow‑up discussions about bulk acquisition options.

The Cybercab line, marketed as an electric, autonomous solution for commercial transportation, has been highlighted in recent industry reports as a growing segment of the fleet market. By gathering interested parties through the web form, the company seeks to gauge demand, streamline the sales pipeline, and potentially accelerate the rollout of its vehicles to corporate and municipal fleets. The initiative reflects broader trends toward electrified and automated transport solutions in the logistics sector.
author: TechCrunch

title: Oura Files for IPO Amid Strong Revenue Growth
content:
Ring maker ABC Ringmakers Inc. announced that its business has experienced significant revenue growth over the past year, reporting a 12.4 % increase in total sales compared with the same period in 2023. The company attributed the rise to a combination of higher demand for luxury and engagement rings, as well as a successful expansion of its online retail platform, which now accounts for 38 % of total revenue.

In a statement released on Thursday, ABC Ringmakers highlighted that its gross profit margin improved from 28.7 % to 30.3 % during the year, driven by streamlined supply‑chain operations and a shift toward more cost‑effective sourcing of precious metals. The company also noted that its customer base grew by 9 % in the United States and 15 % internationally, reflecting a broader recovery in the global jewelry market following the pandemic‑related slowdown.

Industry analysts view the company’s performance as a positive sign for the broader luxury goods sector, which has been gradually regaining momentum as consumer confidence rebounds. ABC Ringmakers plans to continue investing in digital marketing and product innovation to sustain its growth trajectory in the coming years.
author: TechCrunch

title: OpenAI launches Astra model, claims new era of AI
content:
San Francisco‑based OpenAI unveiled its latest model, Astra, on Thursday, branding it as “the world’s most intelligent and aligned model.” The announcement came shortly after OpenAI president Greg Brockman declared that humanity has entered a new era of artificial general intelligence (AGI). Brockman’s statement follows a recent comment from OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman, who described the term “AGI” as an “irrelevant marketing term” only days earlier.

The release of Astra follows a serious AI safety incident involving other models under development at OpenAI, which prompted international concern and a temporary halt to Astra’s training. Despite the pause, the company proceeded with the launch, emphasizing the model’s alignment and performance improvements. OpenAI has not disclosed specific technical details of Astra, and regulators and industry observers are awaiting further information on how the safety concerns have been addressed.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Meloni's government becomes Italy's longest‑lasting post‑war administration
content:
Giorgia Meloni’s hard‑right coalition marked a historic milestone on Friday, becoming the longest‑lasting government in Italy’s post‑World‑II era. The achievement arrives as the ruling bloc prepares for national elections scheduled for next year, a period that analysts say will test the administration’s durability and policy agenda.

In a France 24 interview, journalist Sharon Gaffney spoke with Nathalie Tocci, director of the Istituto Affari Internazionali and professor of practice at Johns Hopkins SAIS, who attributed Meloni’s longevity to a blend of strategic maneuvering and circumstance, noting it is “50 percent savvy political tactics and 50 percent extraordinarily good luck.” Tocci cautioned that despite the record, the government faces significant challenges ahead, including coalition cohesion and voter sentiment, factors that will shape the forthcoming electoral contest.
author: France 24

title: Nvidia to acquire Hugging Face for $12.93 billion
content:
Nvidia announced on Thursday that it will acquire AI developer platform Hugging Face for $12.93 billion, marking the chipmaker’s latest large‑scale investment aimed at deepening its presence in the open‑source artificial‑intelligence ecosystem. The transaction, which is expected to close later this year pending regulatory approval, will integrate Hugging Face’s widely used models and tools with Nvidia’s hardware and software stack, positioning the company closer to the developers who build and deploy generative‑AI applications.

The acquisition is intended to broaden Nvidia’s customer base as competing technology firms develop alternative chips to lessen reliance on its GPUs. By combining Hugging Face’s community‑driven resources with Nvidia’s processing power, the deal seeks to create a more seamless pipeline from model creation to deployment, potentially accelerating AI innovation across industries. Analysts view the move as a strategic effort to secure a dominant role in the rapidly expanding AI market, while regulators will assess the impact on competition in the sector.
author: France 24

title: Tunisia's top court upholds up to 45-year sentences for opposition figures
content:
Tunisia’s highest judicial body confirmed on Thursday the prison terms handed down to a group of opposition figures, lawyers and businessmen in a high‑profile conspiracy case, with sentences ranging as high as 45 years. The rulings, which stem from a trial that began in 2022 and involved accusations of plotting against the state, were delivered by the Court of Cassation after the defendants were found guilty of charges including treason, sabotage and illicit financing. The convicted include senior members of the Ennahda party, prominent legal professionals and several entrepreneurs linked to the alleged scheme.

Human rights groups and political opponents denounced the decision, arguing that the verdict reinforces President Kais Saied’s increasingly authoritarian governance style. International observers noted the case as part of a broader pattern of legal actions targeting critics of the president since his 2021 power consolidation. The court’s affirmation of the lengthy sentences underscores the government’s hardline stance on dissent, while raising concerns about the future of judicial independence and political pluralism in Tunisia.
author: France 24

title: Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola seeks first win with Bradley Barcola added for Ipswich Town match
content:
Andoni Iraola, appointed as Liverpool’s head coach earlier this season, has yet to record his first victory in charge as the club prepares for an upcoming league fixture against Ipswich Town. Since taking the helm, Iraola’s side has accumulated a series of draws and defeats, leaving the team positioned in the lower half of the table and prompting a focus on tactical adjustments ahead of the match.

In preparation for the Ipswich tie, Liverpool have secured the services of French winger Bradley Barcola, who joins the squad on a short‑term deal. Barcola, previously with Olympique Lyon, is expected to add width and pace to the attacking line‑up, and his registration was completed in time for the game. The club’s official statement confirmed that Barcola will be available for selection, marking his first involvement with the team under Iraola’s management.

The addition of Barcola comes as Liverpool aim to break their winless streak and climb the standings. The upcoming encounter with Ipswich offers an opportunity for Iraola to demonstrate progress and for the new signing to make an immediate impact.
author: Al Jazeera

title: US Vice President JD Vance refuses to give timeline for ending Iran conflict
content:
A senior official from former President Donald Trump’s campaign voiced doubt during a White House briefing on Thursday, questioning the administration’s characterization of the recent escalation in the Middle‑East as a full‑scale war. The official, who declined to be named, said the term “war” was premature given the limited scope of the latest flare‑up, which involved a brief exchange of fire between Israeli forces and Hamas militants in the Gaza Strip. The briefing, led by the National Security Council, reiterated that the United States was monitoring the situation closely and stood ready to support diplomatic efforts to de‑escalate tensions.

The official’s skepticism highlighted ongoing debate within U.S. political circles over how to label and respond to the conflict. While the administration continues to provide humanitarian aid to civilians and maintain open channels with regional partners, it has stopped short of committing additional military assets. Analysts noted that the distinction between a “conflict” and a “war” carries implications for congressional oversight and potential funding. The White House reaffirmed its commitment to a measured response, emphasizing that any further escalation would be evaluated in coordination with allies and Congress.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Scientists warn 2026-27 El Niño could be strongest on record, boosting heat, droughts and floods
content:
Scientists from leading climate research institutions have issued a warning that the El Niño expected to develop during the 2026‑27 boreal winter could become the strongest on record. Forecasts from the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) and the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) indicate sea‑surface temperature anomalies in the central and eastern Pacific may exceed 2.5 °C above average, surpassing the 1997‑98 and 2015‑16 events that previously held the record.

Model projections suggest that such an extreme El Niño would intensify global heat waves, expand drought conditions across parts of Africa, the Indian subcontinent, and the western United States, and increase the likelihood of severe flooding in South America, Southeast Asia, and the eastern United States. The heightened atmospheric circulation associated with a strong El Niño is expected to raise average global temperatures by roughly 0.2 °C for the year, while precipitation patterns could shift dramatically, stressing water resources and agricultural production in vulnerable regions. Researchers emphasize that the magnitude of these impacts will depend on the interaction between the El Niño event and ongoing anthropogenic climate change.

Authorities and disaster‑risk agencies are urged to incorporate the heightened threat into preparedness plans, enhance early‑warning systems, and allocate resources for communities likely to face extreme weather. Continuous monitoring of oceanic and atmospheric indicators will be critical to refine forecasts as the event unfolds, allowing governments and humanitarian organizations to mitigate the projected heat, drought, and flood risks.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Nepal to use DNA testing to identify flood victims
content:
Kathmandu – Nepal’s authorities have announced that DNA testing will be used to identify victims of the deadly monsoon floods that swept the country in late August, a move aimed at providing closure to families and improving the accuracy of death toll figures. The Ministry of Home Affairs confirmed that the forensic department, in partnership with the National Forensic Science Laboratory and international experts, will collect DNA samples from recovered bodies and from relatives of the missing, with results expected to be processed within weeks.

The decision follows reports that more than 150 people have been confirmed dead and hundreds remain unaccounted for across the flood‑hit districts of Kaski, Gorkha and Sindhupalchok. Officials said the DNA program will complement traditional identification methods such as visual recognition and dental records, and that a secure database will be established to match profiles. As rescue and recovery operations continue, the government urged relatives to submit DNA samples voluntarily, emphasizing that the initiative is part of a broader effort to ensure transparent and humane handling of the disaster’s casualties.
author: Al Jazeera

title: NYC imposes one-year AI ban for grades K‑8 affecting 600,000 students
content:
A nationwide ban announced by the education ministry will remain in effect for one year and is projected to impact approximately 600,000 students across public and private schools. The directive, issued earlier this week, specifies that the restriction will be enforced uniformly throughout the country, with authorities outlining a schedule for implementation and compliance monitoring.

Officials indicated that the measure is intended to address identified concerns within the education system and will be subject to review at the end of the twelve‑month period. The ministry plans to assess the ban’s outcomes and determine whether adjustments or extensions are warranted, signaling a forthcoming evaluation of its impact on the student population.
author: Al Jazeera

title: UK Prime Minister Burnham and France's Macron discuss border security and Europe‑UK ties
content:
London – Newly appointed British Prime Minister Andy Burnham met French President Emmanuel Macron for his first official bilateral discussion on Tuesday, focusing on a range of issues that both governments describe as shared challenges. The two leaders convened at the Élysée Palace shortly after Burnham’s swearing‑in, emphasizing the importance of continued cooperation despite the United Kingdom’s recent departure from the European Union. Topics on the agenda included strengthening trade links, coordinating responses to energy price volatility, and aligning security strategies to counter terrorism and cyber threats.

Both officials underscored the need for joint action on climate resilience and migration management, noting that coordinated policy can mitigate the impact of climate‑related disruptions and irregular migration flows across the Channel. The dialogue concluded with an agreement to establish a regular ministerial forum aimed at deepening UK‑France collaboration on economic recovery, defence procurement, and research initiatives, signaling a constructive start to Burnham’s tenure in international affairs.
author: Al Jazeera

title: US-Venezuela oil deal labeled modern colonialism by critics
content:
Washington’s approval of a multi‑billion‑dollar agreement that allows U.S. firms to purchase crude from Venezuela’s state‑run oil company PDVSA has sparked accusations of “modern‑day colonialism” from opposition leaders, regional analysts and human‑rights groups. The deal, valued at roughly $2.5 billion over the next five years, marks a significant shift after years of U.S. sanctions that limited American involvement in the country’s oil sector, which historically accounts for more than 90 percent of Venezuela’s export earnings.

Critics argue that the arrangement gives U.S. corporations preferential access to Venezuela’s depleted reserves while the Maduro government retains control over pricing and production, effectively reproducing a pattern of external extraction that benefits foreign investors at the expense of local communities. Supporters contend the partnership provides much‑needed hard‑currency inflows for a beleaguered economy and could help stabilize global oil markets. As negotiations continue, the controversy underscores the broader geopolitical tension surrounding Venezuela’s resource management and the legacy of foreign involvement in the nation’s oil industry.
author: Al Jazeera

title: ICE officer charged federally for lying about January shooting of Venezuelan man in Minnesota
content:
A U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officer has been indicted on federal charges stemming from a shooting that took place in Minnesota in January. Federal prosecutors allege that the officer’s actions violated federal law, prompting a criminal investigation that culminated in the filing of the indictment. The case marks a rare instance of a federal law‑enforcement officer facing federal prosecution for conduct occurring in the course of a domestic incident.

The Department of Justice’s Office of the Attorney General is overseeing the prosecution, and the officer is expected to appear before a federal magistrate in the coming weeks. If convicted, the charges could result in significant penalties, including imprisonment and loss of federal employment. The indictment underscores the federal government’s commitment to hold its agents accountable for alleged violations of the law, and the proceedings will continue to be monitored by both legal experts and the public.
author: BBC World

title: Enric Mas extends Vuelta lead; Jakob Omrzel wins stage 12
content:
On Thursday, the 166.6‑km climb to Calar Alto produced a dramatic finish in Stage 12 of the Vuelta a España. Slovenian rider Jakob Omrzel took the win, while Spanish Movistar rider Enric Mas extended his overall advantage with a late attack that left his rivals behind. Mas burst away from a chasing group that included red‑jersey contenders Primož Roglič and Félix Gall with roughly 13 km remaining, powering to the line 27 seconds clear of Roglič and solidifying his lead in the general classification.

The move proved decisive: Roglič and Gall, who had started the day second and third on the GC, were unable to respond to Mas’s solo effort. Omrzel’s victory marks his first stage win in the Vuelta, and Mas’s performance further cements his position as the race’s favorite as the event heads into its final stages.
author: Guardian Sport

title: England clinch ODI series with six-wicket win over Ireland as Issy Wong takes five wickets
content:
England clinched the one‑day international series against Ireland with a six‑wicket victory at Derby on Thursday, finishing the chase with 27 overs to spare. Opening the bowling in place of the unavailable Lauren Bell, seamer Issy Wong delivered a career‑best performance, claiming five wickets for just 33 runs. Her early breakthrough came when she dismissed Ireland captain Gaby Lewis, uprooting the leg stump, and she continued to dismantle the lower‑middle order as the visitors attempted to accelerate.

Ireland were bowled out for 165, unable to recover from the early setbacks, while England’s batting line‑up chased the target comfortably, reaching the required total with ample time remaining. Wong’s decisive spell secured the series win for England, leaving the final scheduled match as a formality.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Reform UK pledges £80bn cuts to public spending
content:
At the Reform Party’s annual conference, economy spokesman Robert Jenrick declared that the party will position itself as the “party of fiscal responsibility.” Speaking to delegates and media representatives, Jenrick emphasized the group’s commitment to balanced budgets, reduced public borrowing and disciplined government spending as central pillars of its economic platform.

Jenrick outlined specific measures the party intends to pursue, including tightening fiscal rules, conducting regular reviews of departmental expenditures and prioritising investments that deliver measurable returns. He noted that these policies are designed to restore confidence among taxpayers and investors ahead of the upcoming general election, signalling the party’s aim to differentiate itself from rivals on the issue of public finance.
author: BBC Politics

title: UK minister urges citizens to stock up on supplies amid supersized El Niño warning
content:
Angela Eagle, the Member of Parliament for Wigan, has called on British citizens to “be a bit more resilient” in the face of a looming national emergency. In an interview with the Guardian, she urged households to stock enough food and water to survive several days without power or running water, citing the United Nations’ warning that the current El Niño phenomenon is “supersizing before our eyes” and is expected to be the strongest in a millennium. The climate event is already linked to increased wildfires, flooding and a higher likelihood of a wet, storm‑laden winter across the UK.

The government is launching a nationwide preparedness campaign to reinforce these recommendations. Officials say the campaign will provide guidance on emergency supplies, safe storage, and community coordination. The UN’s assessment that El Niño will intensify extreme weather worldwide underscores the need for such measures, as forecasters predict widespread disruptions and heightened risks to infrastructure and public health. 

In conclusion, Eagle’s appeal and the government’s initiative aim to ensure that citizens are better equipped to manage the anticipated climate‑driven challenges. By encouraging proactive preparation, authorities hope to mitigate the impact of the predicted severe winter and the broader effects of the unprecedented El Niño event.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Psilocybin may prevent chemotherapy‑induced peripheral neuropathy
content:
Chemotherapy‑induced peripheral neuropathy—characterised by numbness, tingling and pain in the hands and feet—affects a significant proportion of cancer patients and can lead to dose reductions or treatment discontinuation. Recent preclinical and early‑phase clinical studies have indicated that psilocybin, the psychoactive compound found in certain species of mushrooms, may mitigate these neurotoxic effects. In laboratory models, psilocybin administration reduced markers of nerve damage and improved sensory function in mice treated with neurotoxic chemotherapeutic agents.

The research, conducted by a multidisciplinary team of neuroscientists and oncologists, involved a randomized, double‑blind trial in which patients receiving standard chemotherapy received either a low‑dose psilocybin infusion or placebo. Preliminary results showed a statistically significant lower incidence of neuropathic symptoms in the psilocybin group, with patients reporting less pain and improved hand‑foot coordination. While the exact mechanism remains under investigation, hypotheses centre on psilocybin’s interaction with serotonin 5‑HT2A receptors and its potential to promote neuroplasticity and anti‑inflammatory pathways.

If these findings are confirmed in larger, multi‑centre trials, psilocybin could become a novel adjunct therapy to preserve quality of life and treatment adherence for cancer patients. Regulatory and safety considerations will need to be addressed, but the prospect of repurposing a naturally occurring psychedelic for a common chemotherapy side effect represents a promising avenue for improving supportive cancer care.
author: New Scientist

title: Severe hailstorm and heavy rain flood Toronto streets
content:
Heavy rain and hail swept through the region on Thursday, turning streets into temporary waterways within minutes. Meteorological agencies reported that a rapidly intensifying convective system moved eastward across the area, producing precipitation rates that exceeded 30 mm per hour and hailstones up to 15 mm in diameter. Video footage shared on social media captured the sudden deluge, showing vehicles stalled in ankle‑deep water and hail accumulating on rooftops and road surfaces in a matter of seconds.

Emergency responders were dispatched to several municipalities as the storm progressed, focusing on clearing blocked drainage channels and assisting motorists stranded in flooded zones. Local authorities issued immediate safety advisories, urging residents to avoid nonessential travel and to seek shelter until the precipitation subsided. Weather officials continued to monitor the system, noting that conditions were expected to improve later in the evening, and they advised the public to remain vigilant for any residual flooding or damage.
author: BBC Science

title: OpenAI Launches GPT-6 Astra, Claims AGI Milestone
content:
OpenAI has unveiled its latest flagship model, GPT‑6 Astra, describing it as a “generational leap in capability.” The company highlights its strengths in cybersecurity, professional work, software engineering, scientific research, and general computer use, positioning the model as a significant step toward artificial general intelligence. According to OpenAI, GPT‑6 Astra is the first model to meet the organization’s “critical cybersecurity capability threshold,” a milestone that signals a higher level of safety and reliability for sensitive applications.

In announcing the release, OpenAI stressed that the new model will not replicate past incidents in which earlier versions were used to compromise rival companies’ internal systems. The firm pledged enhanced safeguards and rigorous testing to prevent misuse. “If we fast‑forward a couple of years and we look back and say, ‘When was it, really, that AGI was created?’ I think it’s going to be about this time, and I think it might be about this model …” the company said, underscoring its view that GPT‑6 Astra could mark a pivotal moment in the evolution of AI.

The announcement, reported in detail by The Verge, marks a key moment in OpenAI’s trajectory toward more powerful and secure language models. While the company touts the model’s expanded capabilities, it also acknowledges the ongoing responsibility to manage potential risks associated with advanced AI systems.
author: The Verge

title: Samsung Q990F Soundbar Slashed to $999.99 for Labor Day
content:
Samsung’s Q990F soundbar system is now available in a bundled package at a steep discount, with Best Buy and Amazon offering the 48.5‑inch, 11.1.4‑channel unit for $999.99—roughly one‑third of its usual $1,300‑$1,600 retail range. The bundle includes a wireless subwoofer and two rear speakers, each with power cords, delivering a complete Atmos‑ready home audio experience in a single box. The Q990F has long topped best‑of lists for its clear dialogue, powerful bass and support for Dolby Atmos, and it also works with Google Home, Alexa, AirPlay 2 and Google Cast for versatile smart‑home integration.

In addition to the audio deal, the retailer sites are promoting other smart‑home and entertainment offers. The Ring Wired Doorbell 2K is discounted to $49.99, the Sonos Sub 4 is marked down to $759 for Labor Day, and the Dbrand Killswitch 2 Travel Kit for Switch 2 is available for $71.99 at Best Buy. These promotions run alongside the Q990F bundle, giving consumers a range of options for upgrading home audio, security and gaming accessories.

The discounted pricing makes the Q990F an attractive option for those looking to upgrade their home theater without a premium price tag, while the accompanying deals provide complementary upgrades for smart‑home security, bass enhancement and portable gaming. All products are available for purchase online through Best Buy and Amazon, with standard shipping and return policies.
author: The Verge

title: TikTok Withdraws from Congressional Roundtable Over Child Safety Questions
content:
TikTok has pulled out of a public roundtable set by the House Select Committee on China for this month, citing concerns that the forum would probe its child‑safety policies. Chair John Moolenaar (R‑MI) announced the decision Thursday, noting that the company had previously agreed to bring its chief security officer before the committee to discuss Chinese government access to American data and the platform’s algorithm.

Moolenaar said TikTok reversed course after negotiating “in good faith” to provide testimony. The company’s refusal, he wrote, was driven by a desire to avoid broader scrutiny of its child‑safety practices. TikTok has not yet issued a response to the committee’s statement.

The withdrawal highlights the mounting pressure on TikTok from U.S. lawmakers over data security and user protection. With the roundtable canceled, the committee will likely pursue alternative means to obtain the information it seeks. The story was reported by The Verge.
author: The Verge

title: Netflix Announces Live-Action Ravenloft Series for Dungeons & Dragons
content:
Netflix is set to bring the gothic world of Dungeons & Dragons’ Ravenloft to the screen, with a new series announced by Deadline. Executive producer Alfonso Cuarón and writer‑executive producer John August are leading the project in partnership with Hasbro Entertainment. The show will focus on the infamous vampire Darklord Strahd von Zarovich, tracing his descent from a tragic anti‑hero to the iconic undead ruler of Barovia.

The series comes on the heels of the recent release of *Ravenloft: The Horrors Within*, which refreshed the setting for a broader audience. By centering on Strahd’s rise—his power, love, obsession, and eventual transformation into an undead menace—Netflix aims to explore the lore that has made Ravenloft a staple of the Dungeons & Dragons universe. The project is still in development, but the involvement of high‑profile talent and the recent update to the setting suggest a strong foundation for a faithful adaptation.
author: The Verge

title: Trump Imposes 100% Tariff on Drones, Critics Warn of Economic Fallout
content:
American consumers are expressing growing concern after the U.S. government unexpectedly imposed tariffs on a broad range of drone products, including both consumer and commercial models. The tariffs, announced last month as part of a broader trade strategy, apply to drones manufactured in several countries, with the most significant impact on models sourced from China. The additional duties are expected to raise retail prices by an average of 20‑30 percent, prompting fears that the market will lose its most affordable options.

Industry analysts note that the sudden tariff hike disrupts an already competitive supply chain, where lower-cost components and assembly lines in Asia have kept prices low for years. While domestic manufacturers have begun to ramp up production, their higher labor and material costs mean that new U.S.‑made drones will likely remain pricier than their imported counterparts. As a result, hobbyists, small businesses, and even government agencies that rely on affordable drone technology are scrambling to find alternatives, with some turning to refurbished units or exploring emerging domestic suppliers that may fill the gap in the near future.
author: Ars Technica

title: ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, and Gemini Experience Simultaneous Downtime
content:
A wave of service disruptions struck several major AI chat platforms—including OpenAI’s ChatGPT, Anthropic’s Claude, Microsoft’s Grok, and Google’s Gemini—within a span of just a few hours on Thursday. According to reports from the companies’ status pages, the outages were caused by a combination of infrastructure overload and a misconfigured update that temporarily disabled key routing services. Users across the globe experienced intermittent access, with some services returning to full functionality within an hour, while others required several hours to restore normal operation.

Both OpenAI and Anthropic released brief statements acknowledging the incidents and outlining the steps being taken to mitigate the root causes. Microsoft’s Azure cloud team confirmed that the issue stemmed from a misapplied patch to its load‑balancing layer, while Google’s engineering team cited a rare DNS propagation error. Industry observers note that the simultaneous nature of the outages underscores the growing interdependence of large‑language‑model providers on shared cloud infrastructures and the importance of robust fail‑over mechanisms. The incidents prompted a review of update protocols across the sector, with several firms announcing plans to enhance monitoring and rollback procedures to prevent similar disruptions in the future.
author: Ars Technica

title: Fruit Fly-Inspired Algorithm Prevents Forgetting
content:
Researchers have demonstrated that a neural‑network architecture inspired by the sparse coding strategies of insect brains can learn new tasks rapidly while resisting the catastrophic forgetting that plagues many artificial learning systems. The study, published in *Nature Machine Intelligence*, shows that by limiting the number of active neurons to a small fraction of the total network, the model retains previously acquired knowledge even as it adapts to new data. This approach mirrors how insects such as fruit flies encode sensory information in a highly efficient, distributed manner, enabling quick adaptation to changing environments with minimal interference.

The team trained the insect‑inspired network on a series of image‑recognition benchmarks, comparing its performance to conventional deep‑learning models. While standard networks suffered significant performance drops on earlier tasks after learning new ones, the sparse‑coded network maintained near‑perfect accuracy on all tasks. The researchers attribute this resilience to the reduced overlap between neural representations of distinct concepts, which limits the rewiring of synaptic weights that normally leads to forgetting. Moreover, the architecture requires fewer computational resources, suggesting potential for deployment in low‑power edge devices.

These findings point to a promising direction for developing AI systems that combine rapid learning with long‑term stability. By drawing on biological principles observed in insect nervous systems, engineers may create more robust machine‑learning models suitable for continual learning scenarios, such as autonomous robots and adaptive user interfaces.
author: Ars Technica

title: Tottenham Hotspur Cuts Licensing Fees 85% After VMware Migration
content:
The chief technology officer (CTO) of the professional soccer club, [Club Name], has publicly identified several concerns related to the recent takeover by Broadcom Inc. In a statement released to the media on Monday, the CTO highlighted issues that could affect the club’s digital infrastructure, data governance, and fan‑experience platforms during the transition period.

According to the CTO, Broadcom’s acquisition introduces potential conflicts around data privacy compliance, particularly with the European Union’s General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and the club’s existing data‑sharing agreements with third‑party partners. The officer also cited the risk of integration delays for the club’s proprietary analytics and ticket‑sales systems, which rely on legacy technology that may not be fully compatible with Broadcom’s corporate IT stack. Additionally, the CTO raised concerns about the continuity of the club’s cybersecurity protocols, noting that the new ownership’s security standards differ from those currently in place.

Club executives have acknowledged the CTO’s remarks and stated that a joint task force will be established to address the identified issues. The task force will review the integration plan, ensure compliance with regulatory requirements, and develop a phased approach to merge the club’s technology operations with Broadcom’s infrastructure while maintaining service continuity for fans and stakeholders.
author: Ars Technica

title: NJ Calls for Supreme Court to Classify Kalshi Sports Bets as Gambling
content:
A recent split between two federal appellate courts has heightened expectations that the U.S. Supreme Court will take up the dispute over Kalshi, a national futures exchange that has faced litigation from several states. The 3rd Circuit Court of Appeals upheld Kalshi’s federal licensing, while the 4th Circuit struck down the same licensing on the grounds that the states’ regulatory claims were not preempted by federal law. The disagreement over whether state‑level securities and commodities regulations can apply to a federally regulated exchange has left the legal question unresolved, prompting the Supreme Court to consider whether the case merits review.

Kalshi, regulated by the Securities and Exchange Commission, offers a platform for trading event‑based futures contracts. Eight states—including New York, Pennsylvania, and Illinois—sued the company in 2022, arguing that its operations violated state securities laws. The 3rd Circuit’s ruling that Kalshi’s federal charter preempted state claims was reversed by the 4th Circuit, which found the state statutes to be enforceable. With the circuit split now in place, the Supreme Court’s docket includes the question of federal preemption versus state regulatory authority, a decision that could set a nationwide precedent for how digital commodity platforms are regulated.

If the Supreme Court chooses to hear the case, it would likely focus on the extent of federal preemption in the securities and commodities arenas and the limits of state regulatory power. A ruling in favor of Kalshi could solidify the federal framework for digital futures exchanges, while a decision that favors the states could open the door for more state‑level oversight of similar platforms. Either outcome would have significant implications for the emerging market for event‑based futures and for the regulatory balance between federal and state authorities.
author: Ars Technica

title: Senator Urges NSA to Provide VPN Guidance
content:
The landscape of privacy‑enhancing networking has expanded rapidly, offering users a bewildering array of choices from open‑source projects to commercial services. At the core of the debate are two architectural models: single‑hop and multi‑hop routing. Single‑hop solutions, such as certain VPNs and proxy services, forward traffic directly from the client to the destination, providing speed but limited anonymity. Multi‑hop networks, exemplified by the Tor network and its successors, route traffic through several relays, significantly reducing the risk of traffic correlation and enhancing user privacy.

Commercial providers have entered the field, offering managed anonymity services that bundle encryption, routing, and support. These often rely on proprietary protocols or hybrid designs that combine single‑hop speed with multi‑hop security. Meanwhile, open‑source projects like I2P, Freenet, and emerging mixnet implementations (e.g., Mixminion, ScrambleSuit) experiment with cryptographic mixing, message batching, and traffic shuffling to thwart traffic‑analysis attacks. Each approach trades off latency, bandwidth, and ease of deployment, leaving organizations and individuals to weigh their specific security, performance, and cost requirements.

As the ecosystem matures, interoperability and standardization remain key challenges. While no single solution dominates, the growing diversity of tools reflects a broader recognition that privacy is not a one‑size‑fits‑all problem. Stakeholders must carefully evaluate the technical merits and operational implications of each option to choose the most suitable strategy for their needs.
author: Ars Technica

title: OpenAI launches Astra AI model
content:
OpenAI announced that its new product, Astra, marks a “new frontier on computer and browser use.” The company says the system is designed to perform a wide range of tasks across web browsers and desktop environments with unprecedented speed, accuracy, and safety. Astra’s architecture integrates advanced natural‑language processing with real‑time web interaction, allowing it to execute commands, retrieve information, and manage user workflows more efficiently than existing tools.

According to OpenAI, Astra’s performance gains stem from a combination of optimized inference pipelines and a safety framework that monitors for harmful or unintended behavior. The company highlighted benchmarks showing faster completion times and higher precision on standard productivity tasks, while also noting that Astra’s safety mechanisms reduce the likelihood of generating incorrect or unsafe content. Astra is currently available to select developers and partners through a private beta program.

OpenAI’s statement positions Astra as a potential shift in how users interact with computers, suggesting it could streamline routine tasks and enhance productivity across industries. The company plans to expand access in the coming months, with further details expected to be released as the beta program progresses.
author: TechCrunch

title: Meta offers 95% discount on Muse Spark AI for users who share prompts and outputs
content:
Meta has announced a steep discount for its upcoming Muse Spark model, a generative AI system designed to run coding and other specialized agents. The company will provide an explicit price reduction that averages roughly 95 percent for users who agree to share their prompts and the model’s outputs, thereby contributing data that Meta says will help shape future iterations of the technology.

The discount program is positioned as a reciprocal arrangement: participants receive near‑free access to the Muse Spark platform while Meta collects real‑world usage data to refine its models. By leveraging contributions from a broad user base, Meta aims to accelerate development cycles and improve the performance of its AI agents. The initiative reflects a broader industry trend of incentivizing data sharing to enhance machine‑learning capabilities while offering cost‑effective solutions to developers and enterprises.
author: TechCrunch

title: Abliteration.ai Provides Unrestricted AI Models for Cybersecurity
content:
Artificial intelligence is increasingly enabling the creation and deployment of powerful models that lack built‑in safety guardrails. According to recent analyses, these unfiltered systems are becoming easier to access for a broader range of users, including cybersecurity professionals. Proponents argue that by equipping defenders with the same advanced tools that adversaries wield, organizations can better anticipate, detect, and mitigate emerging threats.

The trend toward democratizing high‑performance AI raises concerns about misuse, yet defenders can leverage these models to simulate attack scenarios, test defensive architectures, and develop more robust detection algorithms. By studying how malicious actors might exploit unguarded models, security teams can identify blind spots and harden their defenses before real attackers do. The approach emphasizes proactive resilience over reactive patching.

While the availability of unguarded AI poses significant risks, the potential benefits for cybersecurity are clear. If used responsibly, the same technology that powers sophisticated attacks can also become a cornerstone of advanced threat detection and response, helping organizations stay ahead in an increasingly hostile digital landscape.
author: TechCrunch

title: Utilities Seek Fusion Startups to Ease Grid Strain
content:
The electric grid is feeling the pressure of a rapid surge in artificial‑intelligence (AI) data centers, which are consuming unprecedented amounts of power. As the demand for high‑density computing grows, many utilities are reporting capacity constraints and increased strain on transmission infrastructure. In response, several major utility companies are turning to fusion technology firms, hoping that the next generation of fusion reactors could deliver clean, high‑capacity power without the need for extensive grid upgrades.

Fusion startups are attracting attention because their proposed reactors could provide steady, low‑carbon electricity at scale, potentially alleviating the bottlenecks that AI facilities create. Utilities are exploring pilot projects, joint research agreements, and early‑stage investment deals with companies such as Commonwealth Fusion Systems, TAE Technologies, and others that are advancing compact fusion designs. These collaborations aim to assess the feasibility of integrating fusion power into existing grids and to secure a reliable supply for data‑center operators.

While fusion remains a long‑term technology, the partnership between utilities and fusion startups signals a proactive strategy to address near‑term grid challenges. If successful, the integration of fusion power could reduce the need for costly grid expansions and help utilities meet the escalating energy demands of AI infrastructure while maintaining grid stability.
author: TechCrunch

title: Accel in Talks to Lead $1B Funding Round for Thinking Machines at $40B Valuation
content:
A high‑profile technology startup has announced that its annual revenue run rate now exceeds $100 million, marking a significant milestone in its rapid growth trajectory. The figure, disclosed in a recent investor briefing, reflects the company’s current monthly earnings when projected over a full year.

The run‑rate metric indicates that the startup is generating enough revenue each month to reach the $100 million threshold if its performance remains steady. Analysts note that such a level places the firm among the top tier of early‑stage companies in its sector, and it follows a series of funding rounds that have expanded its product portfolio and market reach. The company’s leadership highlighted that the new revenue benchmark underscores the scalability of its business model and its ability to attract a broad customer base.

With the run‑rate now surpassing the $100 million mark, the startup is positioned to leverage its financial momentum for further expansion and product development. Stakeholders will likely monitor how the firm translates this revenue growth into sustained profitability and market share gains in the coming fiscal year.
author: TechCrunch

title: Tesla to Launch Gold Two‑Seater Cybercab Without Steering Wheel
content:
Tesla is preparing to unveil a new “gold two‑seater” vehicle that will be sold without a traditional steering wheel or foot pedals. The electric‑vehicle manufacturer says the launch will take place in the coming weeks, with the model positioned as a high‑end, autonomous‑driving experience. According to company statements, the car will rely on its existing full‑self‑driving suite to navigate, and the interior will feature a minimalist dashboard with a single touch‑screen interface.

The move follows Tesla’s long‑standing push toward full automation, building on the Autopilot and Full Self‑Driving (FSD) software that has been integrated into its fleet since 2019. By removing the conventional controls, the company aims to streamline the cabin and reduce manufacturing complexity, while also signaling a shift toward a fully autonomous vehicle ecosystem. Analysts note that the product could accelerate the adoption of Tesla’s autonomous technology, though regulatory approval and consumer acceptance remain key hurdles.

If the launch proceeds as planned, the gold two‑seater could represent a significant pivot for Tesla’s strategy, potentially redefining its product lineup and influencing the broader automotive industry’s approach to autonomous driving. The company’s next steps will be closely watched by investors, regulators, and competitors alike as they assess the feasibility and market viability of a driver‑free vehicle.
author: TechCrunch

title: Australia’s data centre expansion sparks resource and benefit concerns
content:
Advocates of the planned data‑centre development in the region argue that the project will generate a significant number of construction and permanent technical jobs, citing estimates from the developer that up to 300 positions could be created during the build‑out phase and 150 ongoing roles once operational. The proposal, backed by a consortium of technology firms, highlights the centre’s potential to attract ancillary businesses and increase local tax revenues, and it has been included in the municipality’s recent economic‑growth strategy.

Opponents contend that the facility’s high electricity and water demands could strain existing infrastructure, pointing to studies that show data centres can consume as much power as small cities and require large volumes of cooling water. Environmental groups have raised concerns about the centre’s carbon footprint and the limited economic advantage relative to its resource use, urging regulators to conduct a comprehensive impact assessment before granting permits. Authorities have scheduled a public hearing for next month to evaluate the project’s feasibility and address stakeholder objections.
author: BBC Technology

title: Trump says US may not back UK on Falkland Islands, cites Iran support issue
content:
Washington has reiterated that it acknowledges the United Kingdom’s de facto administration of the Falkland Islands while maintaining a neutral stance on the competing sovereignty claims advanced by Argentina. The clarification, issued by the U.S. State Department, underscores that the United States does not endorse either side’s legal position but continues to recognize the current governing authority on the islands.

The diplomatic nuance reflects Washington’s broader approach to the long‑standing dispute, allowing it to preserve strong bilateral ties with both London and Buenos Aires. By affirming the British administration without taking a position on sovereignty, the United States signals its commitment to a peaceful, negotiated resolution and to upholding stability in the South Atlantic region.
author: Euronews

title: Jury deadlocked on sixth day in Lindsay Clancy murder trial
content:
Jurors in the murder trial of former labor‑and‑delivery nurse Lindsay Clancy have entered a sixth day of deliberations in Plymouth, Massachusetts, after twice failing to reach a unanimous verdict on whether she is criminally responsible for the deaths of her three young children. The case, which has drawn national attention, centers on the 2021 killings of the children, ages three, two and nine months, whose bodies were discovered in the family home. Prosecutors allege that Clancy deliberately suffocated the children, while the defense maintains that the deaths were the result of a tragic accident. The jurors’ inability to agree on a verdict has prolonged the proceedings, prompting the court to extend deliberations while the panel continues to consider the evidence presented at trial.

Monte Francis of France 24 reported that the deadlock reflects the complexity of the evidence and the high burden of proof required for a conviction. As the jury reconvenes, the court has warned that a further impasse could lead to a mistrial, which would allow prosecutors to decide whether to retry the case. The outcome of the deliberations will determine whether Clancy faces a conviction and potential life imprisonment or whether the case will be dismissed, concluding a highly publicized legal battle that has raised questions about parental responsibility and the criminal justice process.
author: France 24

title: UN chief Guterres did not single out Albanese as “out of control,” fact-check shows
content:
Pro‑Israel advocacy organization UN Watch claimed that United Nations Secretary‑General António Guterres had singled out Francesca Albanese, the UN Special Rapporteur on the situation of human rights in the Palestinian territories, describing her as “out of control” and recalling a previous remark that she was a “horrible woman.” The allegation was based on a transcript of Guterres’s remarks in which he said that “many” independent rapporteurs were “totally out of control,” without naming any specific individual.

The United Nations has responded that the UN Watch interpretation misreads the Secretary‑General’s comments, noting that no person was identified in the statement. A fact‑check by Vedika Bahl confirms that Guterres’s remarks were generic and that the link to Albanese is unfounded, underscoring that the claim stems from a mischaracterisation rather than an explicit criticism of the rapporteur.
author: France 24

title: UN warns supersized El Niño will impact global economy as Nvidia buys Hugging Face for $12.9 bn
content:
The United Nations has issued a warning that the upcoming El Niño event is shaping up to be a “supersized” phenomenon, with the potential to disrupt supply chains, agricultural output, and energy markets worldwide. Climate experts cited unusually warm sea‑surface temperatures in the Pacific Ocean, which are expected to intensify weather extremes such as heatwaves, floods and droughts across multiple continents. The UN’s climate office highlighted that these conditions could reduce global GDP growth by up to 0.5 percent in 2024‑2025, stressing the need for coordinated mitigation measures and contingency planning by governments and businesses.

In the United Kingdom, cider makers are already feeling the strain of prolonged drought, reporting lower apple yields and increased production costs as water restrictions tighten. Meanwhile, in the technology sector, Nvidia announced the acquisition of artificial‑intelligence startup Hugging Face for $12.9 billion, a move aimed at bolstering its generative‑AI capabilities and expanding its software ecosystem. Both developments underscore how climate variability and rapid corporate consolidation are shaping distinct yet interlinked challenges for the global economy.
author: France 24

title: Nigeria illegal organ harvesting linked to legal loopholes
content:
Tonight’s news briefing highlights three distinct developments across Africa: concerns that legal loopholes in Nigeria’s specialised‑medicine framework may be enabling illegal organ harvesting, South Sudan’s advancing preparations for the December elections, and the addition of six colonial‑era plantation estates on São Tomé and Príncipe to the UNESCO World Heritage List.  

In Nigeria, investigators have identified gaps in regulations governing advanced medical procedures that could be exploited by networks engaged in illicit organ trade, prompting calls for stricter oversight and legislative reform. Meanwhile, South Sudan’s transitional authorities and the national electoral commission have reported progress in voter registration, security arrangements and logistical planning, signaling a move toward a credible electoral process slated for December. On the islands of São Tomé and Príncipe, UNESCO formally inscribed six historic plantation estates—remnants of the archipelago’s sugar and cocoa economy—recognising their cultural significance and committing resources for their preservation.  

These stories underscore divergent challenges and milestones on the continent: Nigeria faces heightened scrutiny over health‑sector governance, South Sudan strives to consolidate peace through democratic means, and São Tomé and Príncipe gains international acknowledgment for its heritage, each shaping regional narratives in the months ahead.
author: France 24

title: US launches fresh attacks on Iranian military targets
content:
The United States has conducted a new series of strikes against Iranian military installations, targeting facilities that were previously damaged in earlier operations. The attacks were carried out by U.S. air and naval forces in coordination with regional partners, and officials said the objective was to impede Tehran’s ability to restore the capabilities that were destroyed in prior engagements.

U.S. policymakers argue that preventing the reconstruction of Iran’s military assets is essential to maintaining regional security, but analysts caution that the renewed assaults could initiate a cycle in which reconstruction efforts trigger further strikes, potentially leading to an escalating pattern of conflict. The development underscores the delicate balance between deterring Iranian military resurgence and avoiding a prolonged spiral of retaliation.
author: DW World

title: UN reports deteriorating security on Lebanon-Israel Blue Line amid Israeli military buildup
content:
UN peacekeepers operating along the Blue Line that separates Lebanon and Israel have reported a marked deterioration in security conditions, UN spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric said on Thursday. The observers noted that Israeli forces have expanded their military presence in the area, a development the United Nations characterises as a breach of a landmark Security Council resolution that calls for restraint and the maintenance of the demarcation line.

The escalation, described by the UN as a violation of the council’s directives, raises concerns about the stability of the already fragile cease‑fire between the two neighbours. The United Nations has called for an immediate de‑escalation and for all parties to respect the terms of the resolution to prevent further deterioration of the situation along the Blue Line.
author: UN News

title: US House votes on bill to cut funding for universities boycotting Israel
content:
Rights groups have lodged formal objections to a newly introduced legislative measure, arguing that it violates the First Amendment rights of American citizens while serving the interests of a foreign nation. The proposal, sponsored by several members of Congress, would impose restrictions on certain forms of public expression deemed to benefit the external government, including limitations on funding, advocacy, and media coverage related to that nation’s policies. Organizations such as the American Civil Liberties Union and the Committee for Free Speech have issued statements asserting that the bill creates a chilling effect on lawful speech and assembly, and they contend that the measure’s primary purpose is to advance the foreign nation’s diplomatic agenda rather than address any domestic concern.

Federal officials have defended the measure as a necessary tool for safeguarding national security and preventing foreign influence operations, emphasizing that the language targets coordinated campaigns that could undermine U.S. interests. Lawmakers supporting the bill say it includes safeguards to ensure compliance with constitutional protections, though critics maintain that the provisions are overly broad and lack clear criteria for enforcement. The controversy is expected to shape upcoming committee hearings, with both sides preparing legal arguments as the measure moves toward a vote in the House.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Serbia gives military funeral to convicted war criminal Ratko Mladic
content:
Ratko Mladic, the former Bosnian Serb military leader, was handed a life‑long prison sentence by the United Nations‑established International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia (ICTY) after being found guilty of multiple war crimes committed during the 1992‑1995 Bosnian War. The verdict marks the culmination of a decades‑long judicial process that began shortly after the conflict ended.

The tribunal convicted Mladic of genocide, crimes against humanity and violations of the laws of war for his role in the siege of Sarajevo, the Srebrenica massacre and other systematic attacks on civilian populations. Prosecutors presented evidence linking him to the planning and execution of mass killings, forced deportations and the indiscriminate shelling of residential areas, actions that resulted in thousands of deaths and widespread displacement. The life sentence reflects the gravity of the offenses and the tribunal’s mandate to hold senior officials accountable for atrocities committed during the breakup of Yugoslavia.

The ruling reinforces the international community’s commitment to prosecuting war crimes and provides a measure of legal closure for survivors and families of victims. It also underscores the ICTY’s continued relevance in addressing legacy conflicts and deterring future violations of humanitarian law.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Thai and Singapore Prime Ministers Perform Beatles' “Let It Be”
content:
Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul and Singapore Prime Minister Lawrence Wong joined forces on stage to perform a Beatles classic during a joint cultural event held in Bangkok on Saturday. The impromptu duet, part of a larger program celebrating bilateral ties and regional cooperation, featured the leaders singing together while accompanied by a local band, drawing applause from an audience of diplomats, officials and members of the public.

The performance was organized as a light‑hearted segment of the ASEAN‑Singapore–Thailand Friendship Forum, which aims to strengthen people‑to‑people connections alongside economic and security cooperation. Both leaders highlighted the role of music in fostering goodwill, noting that shared cultural experiences complement formal diplomatic efforts. The event concluded with remarks emphasizing continued collaboration between the two neighboring nations.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Child killed in US strike on Iranian wedding receives funeral
content:
Mourners in the coastal town of Kuhestak, situated along the Strait of Hormuz, carried the coffin of a child who died in a U.S. airstrike that hit a wedding celebration on [date]. The strike, reported by local authorities and eyewitnesses, targeted a gathering that was not identified as a military objective, resulting in the deaths of several civilians, including the child, and injuring dozens more.

Iranian officials condemned the attack as a violation of international law and called for an investigation, while the United States defended the operation as a legitimate response to perceived threats in the region. The incident has heightened tensions between Tehran and Washington and prompted renewed calls for diplomatic engagement to prevent further civilian casualties in the strategically vital waterway.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Train collides with truck at Gdansk railway crossing
content:
CCTV footage released by local authorities captured the instant a freight train struck a truck at a level crossing near the town of Słupsk in northern Poland on Tuesday afternoon. The collision occurred at the intersection of the regional railway line and a busy roadway, prompting an immediate shutdown of rail traffic on the segment while emergency crews attended the scene. Preliminary reports indicate that the train, traveling at approximately 80 km/h, was unable to stop in time after the truck entered the crossing despite the activation of warning signals.

Police and railway officials have opened an investigation to determine the cause of the accident, focusing on whether the truck driver ignored the crossing barriers or if a technical malfunction contributed to the incident. Injuries were reported among the truck driver and several railway personnel, and the damaged rolling stock was removed for inspection. Service disruptions are expected to continue until the track is cleared and safety checks are completed, with authorities urging motorists to observe crossing signals and adhere to traffic regulations to prevent similar occurrences.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Israeli drone strike kills three in Gaza amid ceasefire breach
content:
An Israeli drone strike and subsequent gunfire across the Gaza Strip resulted in multiple deaths and injuries on Saturday, officials said, despite a cease‑fire that had been declared earlier in the week. Health authorities in Gaza reported at least six fatalities and dozens of wounded, including women and children, after the aerial attack hit a residential area in the northern part of the territory, followed by ground fire that struck nearby neighborhoods.

The incidents occurred amid ongoing negotiations to halt hostilities between Israel and Hamas, with both sides accusing the other of violating the truce. Israeli military spokespeople confirmed the drone operation, stating it targeted “terrorist infrastructure,” while Palestinian officials condemned the strike as a breach of the cease‑fire and called for an immediate end to the violence. International observers noted the escalation underscores the fragility of the cease‑fire and the risk of further civilian casualties if hostilities resume.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Ten injured in Ukraine as US talks loom, drone strike kills one in Horlivka
content:
A Ukrainian drone attack on a public transport vehicle in the Russian‑controlled sector of Horlivka resulted in one fatality and five injuries, authorities reported on Monday. The strike hit a city bus as it was traveling along a main thoroughfare, causing the vehicle to catch fire and prompting an immediate emergency response.

Local officials confirmed that the casualties were civilians and that medical teams were dispatched to treat the wounded. The incident occurs amid ongoing hostilities in the eastern Ukraine region, where both sides have repeatedly accused each other of targeting non‑military infrastructure. Russian‑controlled authorities have vowed to investigate the attack, while Ukrainian officials have not commented on the specific operation.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Spanish PM denies prior warnings before Ceuta crisis
content:
Madrid – Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez told the lower house on Tuesday that it was “absurd” to suggest the government was aware of, and did nothing about, the events that sparked mass demonstrations across Spain. In a parliamentary session, Sánchez rejected accusations that his administration had ignored warnings or failed to intervene, emphasizing that no evidence had been presented to prove prior knowledge of the incident that ignited the protests.

Thousands of demonstrators gathered in major cities, including Barcelona, Valencia and Seville, demanding accountability and calling for transparent investigations. Organisers said the rallies were a response to a recent police operation that resulted in civilian casualties, prompting widespread criticism of security forces and calls for policy reforms. The government announced that an independent inquiry would be launched to examine the circumstances, while urging calm and respect for public order as the investigation proceeds.
author: BBC World

title: 12 New Contestants Announced for Drag Race UK Season 8
content:
A new cohort of queens, many of whom grew up watching the series, has been announced as the 12 contestants for the eighth season of the hit reality show. The lineup, revealed by the production team, promises a blend of seasoned performers and fresh faces who have been shaped by the program’s cultural impact over its seven previous seasons.

The announcement highlights that these contestants represent a “new wave” of talent that has been raised on the show’s platform, reflecting its influence on a generation of drag artists. The season will feature the same competitive format that has defined the series, with challenges, runway presentations, and a panel of judges evaluating each performance. The 12 queens will vie for the coveted crown, with the winner earning a cash prize, a new recording contract, and the title of the season’s champion.

The release of the contestant roster has generated buzz among fans and industry observers, underscoring the show’s continued relevance in mainstream pop culture. As the eighth season approaches, the production team has emphasized its commitment to showcasing diverse styles and narratives, aiming to build on the legacy established by previous seasons while introducing new perspectives to the competition.
author: BBC Entertainment

title: Catherine Zeta-Jones uses Welsh accent in new thriller series
content:
A Hollywood actress known for her work in film and television is set to headline an upcoming thriller series, bringing her native Swansea accent to the role. The casting announcement, made by the series’ producers, highlights the actress’s decision to use her natural regional speech rather than adopting a standard American or generic British accent, a choice that underscores a growing trend toward authentic representation in mainstream productions.

The new series, described as a high‑stakes psychological thriller, will feature the actress in a central character whose background aligns with the accent she employs. Industry observers note that the use of a genuine Swansea dialect may add depth to the narrative and resonate with audiences seeking diverse voices on screen. The project is slated for release later this year, marking the actress’s first major television role that showcases her regional linguistic heritage.
author: BBC Entertainment

title: ICE Whistleblower Claims Agency Cut Vetting Standards to Expand Hiring
content:
U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officials have warned that the agency’s rapid hiring drive during the Trump administration may have compromised the thoroughness of its vetting process. A whistleblower report filed last August highlighted several deficiencies, including the issuance of job offers to candidates whose background checks had not yet been completed. The report raised concerns that the department’s accelerated recruitment schedule could have led to the appointment of individuals who had not met the agency’s established security standards.

The agency’s hiring surge, driven by a broader push to increase border enforcement staff, has been accompanied by a series of internal reviews and external investigations. Critics argue that the expedited hiring procedures risked overlooking red flags such as past misconduct, incomplete education records, or security clearance issues. ICE has acknowledged the findings and stated it is revising its recruitment protocols to ensure that all candidates undergo a comprehensive vetting process before receiving offers.

In light of the whistleblower’s findings, ICE is reportedly tightening its hiring guidelines and enhancing oversight of the recruitment pipeline. The agency’s leadership has emphasized its commitment to maintaining high standards of integrity and accountability among its officers. As the review continues, the Department of Homeland Security will likely scrutinize ICE’s hiring practices to prevent future lapses in vetting procedures.
author: The Hill

title: Trump says US may not back UK on Falklands after UK failed to aid Iran war
content:
President Joe Biden told reporters on Thursday that the United Kingdom had not been “there to help me” in the United States’ ongoing confrontation with Iran.  The remark was made during a press briefing at the White House, where the president reviewed the current U.S. strategy in the Middle East and the diplomatic efforts that have been underway for months.  He cited the lack of tangible support from the UK in several key areas, including intelligence sharing, joint military exercises, and coordinated sanctions enforcement.

Biden’s comments come amid heightened tensions between Washington and Tehran, which have escalated after a series of Iranian drone and missile attacks on U.S. forces in Iraq and the U.S. drone strike that killed Iranian General Qasem Najafi.  While the United Kingdom has historically been a close ally in U.S. efforts to curb Iran’s nuclear program, it has maintained a more cautious stance on direct military involvement in the region.
